title: Advanced Ex-situ and In-situ Electron Microscopy Characterization of Fusion Plasma-Facing Tungsten Oxidation
content: To achieve sustainable carbon-free fusion energy, it is crucial to understand the degradation of reactor structural materials under both normal operating conditions and potential accident scenarios. Tungsten (W), a key plasma-facing material (PFM), is highly susceptible to severe high-temperature oxidation in case of loss-of-vacuum (LOVA) and loss-of-coolant (LOCA) accidents in fusion reactors. However, how pre-existing irradiation damage impacts W oxidation process and kinetics is poorly understood. In addition to radiation effects, our previous in-situ environmental TEM (ETEM) study revealed that W oxidation behavior is strongly influenced by the grain orientation of the metal surface [1]. This talk will present our recent efforts to address these fundamental challenges using a combination of in-situ ETEM oxidation, stepwise thermogravimetric analysis (TGA), and post-oxidation characterization via a combination of SEM, TEM and atomic force microscopy (AFM).
